parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **globalisation**?
choices: Investment by a firm in one country in productive assets such as factories or businesses in another country
A firm that has its headquarters in one country and production or service operations in at least one other country
The reduction or removal of barriers to international trade such as tariffs and quotas
The growing integration and interdependence of the world's economies through trade, investment, people and information

rows.answer:

intro:
Global trade has reached record levels, although growth has slowed recently. Consumers in Malaysia can now buy products from around the world, often online, and many international brands have opened stores in Penang.

Imports make up 39% of goods bought in Malaysia. The average price of clothing and electronics has fallen by 20% in real terms over ten years. Online purchases from foreign websites rose by 19% last year.

However, 35,000 manufacturing jobs have been lost in Malaysia over the same period. Some local brands have closed, and consumer groups have raised concerns about the quality and safety of some cheap imports.

intro:
Many clothing factories in Pradesia produce goods for international brands. Wages are low, but the industry employs over 2 million people, mainly women.

Clothing makes up 61% of Pradesia's exports. Average wages in the factories are about US\$145 a month, higher than in agriculture. A factory fire five years ago killed 52 workers.

Some international brands have since agreed to safety inspections. Other countries in the region are now attracting clothing firms with even lower wages.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **free trade**?
choices: When a country can produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country
When a country can produce more of a good than another country using the same resources
International trade that takes place without barriers such as tariffs or quotas
Goods and services produced in one country and sold to buyers in other countries

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (International trade that takes place without barriers such as tariffs or quotas)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of comparative advantage
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of absolute advantage
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of exports

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **protectionism**?
choices: A new domestic industry that is not yet able to compete with established foreign firms
The use of barriers to trade to protect domestic firms from foreign competition
A group of countries with free trade between members and a common external tariff on non-members
An international organisation that sets the rules of trade between countries and aims to reduce trade barriers

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The use of barriers to trade to protect domestic firms from foreign competition)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of infant industry
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of customs union
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of World Trade Organization (WTO)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **tariff**?
choices: An international organisation that sets the rules of trade between countries and aims to reduce trade barriers
Selling goods abroad at a price below their cost of production
A tax placed on imported goods
A new domestic industry that is not yet able to compete with established foreign firms

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (A tax placed on imported goods)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of World Trade Organization (WTO)
